BatchExecuteStatement.name: BatchExecuteStatement
BatchExecuteStatement.doc: This operation allows you to perform batch reads or writes on data stored in DynamoDB, using PartiQL. Each read statement in a BatchExecuteStatement must specify an equality condition on all key attributes. This enforces that each SELECT statement in a batch returns at most a single item. For more information, see Running batch operations with PartiQL for DynamoDB . The entire batch must consist…

BatchGetItem.name: BatchGetItem
BatchGetItem.doc: The BatchGetItem operation returns the attributes of one or more items from one or more tables. You identify requested items by primary key. A single operation can retrieve up to 16 MB of data, which can contain as many as 100 items. BatchGetItem returns a partial result if the response size limit is exceeded, the table's provisioned throughput is exceeded, more than 1MB per partition is…

BatchWriteItem.name: BatchWriteItem
BatchWriteItem.doc: The BatchWriteItem operation puts or deletes multiple items in one or more tables. A single call to BatchWriteItem can transmit up to 16MB of data over the network, consisting of up to 25 item put or delete operations. While individual items can be up to 400 KB once stored, it's important to note that an item's representation might be greater than 400KB while being sent in DynamoDB's JSON format…

CreateBackup.name: CreateBackup
CreateBackup.doc: Creates a backup for an existing table. Each time you create an on-demand backup, the entire table data is backed up. There is no limit to the number of on-demand backups that can be taken. When you create an on-demand backup, a time marker of the request is cataloged, and the backup is created asynchronously, by applying all changes until the time of the request to the last full table snapshot.…

CreateGlobalTable.name: CreateGlobalTable
CreateGlobalTable.doc: Creates a global table from an existing table. A global table creates a replication relationship between two or more DynamoDB tables with the same table name in the provided Regions. This documentation is for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables, which should be avoided for new global tables. Customers should use Global Tables version 2019.11.21 (Current) when possible, because it…

CreateTable.name: CreateTable
CreateTable.doc: The CreateTable operation adds a new table to your account. In an Amazon Web Services account, table names must be unique within each Region. That is, you can have two tables with same name if you create the tables in different Regions. CreateTable is an asynchronous operation. Upon receiving a CreateTable request, DynamoDB immediately returns a response with a TableStatus of CREATING. After the…

DeleteBackup.name: DeleteBackup
DeleteBackup.doc: Deletes an existing backup of a table. You can call DeleteBackup at a maximum rate of 10 times per second.

DeleteItem.name: DeleteItem
DeleteItem.doc: Deletes a single item in a table by primary key. You can perform a conditional delete operation that deletes the item if it exists, or if it has an expected attribute value. In addition to deleting an item, you can also return the item's attribute values in the same operation, using the ReturnValues parameter. DeleteResourcePolicy.doc: Deletes the resource-based policy attached to the resource, which can be a table or stream. DeleteResourcePolicy is an idempotent operation; running it multiple times on the same resource doesn't result in an error response, unless you specify an ExpectedRevisionId, which will then return a PolicyNotFoundException. To make sure that you don't inadvertently lock yourself out of your own resources,…

DeleteTable.name: DeleteTable
DeleteTable.doc: The DeleteTable operation deletes a table and all of its items. After a DeleteTable request, the specified table is in the DELETING state until DynamoDB completes the deletion. If the table is in the ACTIVE state, you can delete it. If a table is in CREATING or UPDATING states, then DynamoDB returns a ResourceInUseException. If the specified table does not exist, DynamoDB returns a…

DescribeBackup.name: DescribeBackup
DescribeBackup.doc: Describes an existing backup of a table. You can call DescribeBackup at a maximum rate of 10 times per second.

DescribeContinuousBackups.doc: Checks the status of continuous backups and point in time recovery on the specified table. Continuous backups are ENABLED on all tables at table creation. DescribeContributorInsights.name: DescribeContributorInsights
DescribeContributorInsights.doc: Returns information about contributor insights for a given table or global secondary index.

DescribeEndpoints.name: DescribeEndpoints
DescribeEndpoints.doc: Returns the regional endpoint information. For more information on policy permissions, please see Internetwork traffic privacy.

DescribeGlobalTable.doc: Returns information about the specified global table. This documentation is for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables, which should be avoided for new global tables. DescribeImport.doc: Represents the properties of the import.

DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination.name: DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination
DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination.doc: Returns information about the status of Kinesis streaming.

DescribeLimits.doc: Returns the current provisioned-capacity quotas for your Amazon Web Services account in a Region, both for the Region as a whole and for any one DynamoDB table that you create there. DescribeTable.name: DescribeTable
DescribeTable.doc: Returns information about the table, including the current status of the table, when it was created, the primary key schema, and any indexes on the table. DescribeTableReplicaAutoScaling.name: DescribeTableReplicaAutoScaling
DescribeTableReplicaAutoScaling.doc: Describes auto scaling settings across replicas of the global table at once.

DescribeTimeToLive.name: DescribeTimeToLive
DescribeTimeToLive.doc: Gives a description of the Time to Live (TTL) status on the specified table.

DisableKinesisStreamingDestination.name: DisableKinesisStreamingDestination
DisableKinesisStreamingDestination.doc: Stops replication from the DynamoDB table to the Kinesis data stream. This is done without deleting either of the resources.

EnableKinesisStreamingDestination.name: EnableKinesisStreamingDestination
EnableKinesisStreamingDestination.doc: Starts table data replication to the specified Kinesis data stream at a timestamp chosen during the enable workflow. If this operation doesn't return results immediately, use DescribeKinesisStreamingDestination to check if streaming to the Kinesis data stream is ACTIVE.

ExecuteStatement.doc: This operation allows you to perform reads and singleton writes on data stored in DynamoDB, using PartiQL. For PartiQL reads (SELECT statement), if the total number of processed items exceeds the maximum dataset size limit of 1 MB, the read stops and results are returned to the user as a LastEvaluatedKey value to continue the read in a subsequent operation. ExecuteTransaction.doc: This operation allows you to perform transactional reads or writes on data stored in DynamoDB, using PartiQL. ExportTableToPointInTime.name: ExportTableToPointInTime
ExportTableToPointInTime.doc: Exports table data to an S3 bucket. The table must have point in time recovery enabled, and you can export data from any time within the point in time recovery window.

GetItem.name: GetItem
GetItem.doc: The GetItem operation returns a set of attributes for the item with the given primary key. If there is no matching item, GetItem does not return any data and there will be no Item element in the response. GetItem provides an eventually consistent read by default. ImportTable.name: ImportTable
ImportTable.doc: Imports table data from an S3 bucket.

ListBackups.doc: List DynamoDB backups that are associated with an Amazon Web Services account and weren't made with Amazon Web Services Backup. ListImports.name: ListImports

ListTables.name: ListTables
ListTables.doc: Returns an array of table names associated with the current account and endpoint. The output from ListTables is paginated, with each page returning a maximum of 100 table names.

ListTagsOfResource.doc: List all tags on an Amazon DynamoDB resource. You can call ListTagsOfResource up to 10 times per second, per account. For an overview on tagging DynamoDB resources, see Tagging for DynamoDB in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide.

PutItem.doc: Creates a new item, or replaces an old item with a new item. PutResourcePolicy.name: PutResourcePolicy
PutResourcePolicy.doc: Attaches a resource-based policy document to the resource, which can be a table or stream. Query.doc: You must provide the name of the partition key attribute and a single value for that attribute. Query returns all items with that partition key value. Optionally, you can provide a sort key attribute and use a comparison operator to refine the search results. RestoreTableFromBackup.name: RestoreTableFromBackup
RestoreTableFromBackup.doc: Creates a new table from an existing backup. Any number of users can execute up to 50 concurrent restores (any type of restore) in a given account. You can call RestoreTableFromBackup at a maximum rate of 10 times per second. RestoreTableToPointInTime.name: RestoreTableToPointInTime
RestoreTableToPointInTime.doc: Restores the specified table to the specified point in time within EarliestRestorableDateTime and LatestRestorableDateTime. Scan.name: Scan
Scan.doc: The Scan operation returns one or more items and item attributes by accessing every item in a table or a secondary index. To have DynamoDB return fewer items, you can provide a FilterExpression operation. SearchVectors.doc: Performs a vector similarity search on a vector index associated with an Amazon DynamoDB table, and returns the most similar items sorted by similarity score based on the distance function configured for the index. TransactGetItems.name: TransactGetItems
TransactGetItems.doc: TransactGetItems is a synchronous operation that atomically retrieves multiple items from one or more tables (but not from indexes) in a single account and Region. TransactWriteItems.doc: TransactWriteItems is a synchronous write operation that groups up to 100 action requests. UntagResource.name: UntagResource
UntagResource.doc: Removes the association of tags from an Amazon DynamoDB resource. You can call UntagResource up to five times per second, per account. UntagResource is an asynchronous operation. UpdateContinuousBackups.name: UpdateContinuousBackups
UpdateContinuousBackups.doc: UpdateContinuousBackups enables or disables point in time recovery for the specified table. UpdateContributorInsights.doc: Updates the status for contributor insights for a specific table or index. UpdateGlobalTable.name: UpdateGlobalTable
UpdateGlobalTable.doc: Adds or removes replicas in the specified global table. The global table must already exist to be able to use this operation. Any replica to be added must be empty, have the same name as the global table, have the same key schema, have DynamoDB Streams enabled, and have the same provisioned and maximum write capacity units. UpdateGlobalTableSettings.doc: Updates settings for a global table. This documentation is for version 2017.11.29 (Legacy) of global tables, which should be avoided for new global tables. UpdateItem.name: UpdateItem
UpdateItem.doc: Edits an existing item's attributes, or adds a new item to the table if it does not already exist. You can put, delete, or add attribute values. UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination.name: UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination
UpdateKinesisStreamingDestination.doc: The command to update the Kinesis stream destination.

UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling.name: UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling
UpdateTableReplicaAutoScaling.doc: Updates auto scaling settings on your global tables at once.

UpdateTimeToLive.name: UpdateTimeToLive
UpdateTimeToLive.doc: The UpdateTimeToLive method enables or disables Time to Live (TTL) for the specified table. A successful UpdateTimeToLive call returns the current TimeToLiveSpecification. S.doc: An attribute of type String. For example: "S": "Hello"

N.doc: An attribute of type Number. For example: "N": "123.45" Numbers are sent across the network to DynamoDB as strings, to maximize compatibility across languages and libraries. However, DynamoDB treats them as number type attributes for mathematical operations.

B.doc: An attribute of type Binary. For example: "B": "dGhpcyB0ZXh0IGlzIGJhc2U2NC1lbmNvZGVk"

SS.doc: An attribute of type String Set. For example: "SS": ["Giraffe", "Hippo" ,"Zebra"]

M.doc: An attribute of type Map. For example: "M": {"Name": {"S": "Joe"}, "Age": {"N": "35"}}

L.doc: An attribute of type List. For example: "L": [ {"S": "Cookies"} , {"S": "Coffee"}, {"N": "3.14159"}]

NULL.doc: An attribute of type Null. For example: "NULL": true

BOOL.doc: An attribute of type Boolean. For example: "BOOL": true

StreamSpecification.doc: Represents the DynamoDB Streams configuration for the table. You receive a ValidationException if you try to enable a stream on a table that already has a stream, or if you try to disable a stream on a table that doesn't have a stream.

SSESpecification.doc: The new server-side encryption settings for the specified table.

ReplicaUpdates.doc: A list of replica update actions (create, delete, or update) for the table.

TableClass.doc: The table class of the table to be updated. Valid values are STANDARD and STANDARD_INFREQUENT_ACCESS.

DeletionProtectionEnabled.doc: Indicates whether deletion protection is to be enabled (true) or disabled (false) on the table.

MultiRegionConsistency.doc: Specifies the consistency mode for a new global table. OnDemandThroughput.doc: Updates the maximum number of read and write units for the specified table in on-demand capacity mode. If you use this parameter, you must specify MaxReadRequestUnits, MaxWriteRequestUnits, or both.

WarmThroughput.doc: Represents the warm throughput (in read units per second and write units per second) for updating a table.

GlobalTableSettingsReplicationMode.doc: Controls the settings replication mode for a global table replica. This attribute can be defined using UpdateTable operation only on a regional table with values: ENABLED: Defines settings replication on a regional table to be used as a source table for creating Multi-Account Global Table. VectorIndexUpdates.doc: A list of vector indexes to be added to or removed from the table. You can add or remove one vector index for each UpdateTable operation. To add a vector index, specify IndexName, VectorAttribute, Dimensions, DistanceFunction, and Projection. To remove a vector index, specify only the IndexName.

UpdateTableInput.doc: Represents the input of an UpdateTable operation.

TableDescription.doc: Represents the properties of the table.

UpdateTableOutput.doc: Represents the output of an UpdateTable operation.

GlobalSecondaryIndexUpdates.doc: Represents the auto scaling settings of the global secondary indexes of the replica to be updated.

TableName.doc: The name of the global table to be updated. You can also provide the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the table in this parameter.

ReplicaUpdates.doc: Represents the auto scaling settings of replicas of the table that will be modified.

TableAutoScalingDescription.doc: Returns information about the auto scaling settings of a table with replicas.

TableName.doc: The name of the table to be configured. You can also provide the Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the table in this parameter.

TimeToLiveSpecification.doc: Represents the settings used to enable or disable Time to Live for the specified table.

UpdateTimeToLiveInput.doc: Represents the input of an UpdateTimeToLive operation.

TimeToLiveSpecification.doc: Represents the output of an UpdateTimeToLive operation.

AttributeName.doc: The name of the vector attribute.

VectorAttributeDefinition.doc: The definition of a vector attribute for a vector index.

VectorSearchRequestBytes.doc: The number of vector search request bytes consumed by a SearchVectors operation.

VectorWriteRequestBytes.doc: The number of vector write request bytes consumed when writing to a vector index. Reported for write operations that modify attributes indexed by a vector index.

VectorCapacity.doc: The consumed capacity for vector index operations, including vector search request bytes and vector write request bytes.

IndexName.doc: The name of the vector index.

VectorAttribute.doc: The vector attribute configuration for the index.

SearchSchema.doc: The search schema that defines partition key and inline filter attributes for the vector index.

Projection.doc: Specifies attributes that are copied (projected) from the table into the vector index.

Dimensions.doc: The number of dimensions in each vector.

DistanceFunction.doc: The distance function used to calculate similarity between vectors. Valid values: COSINE, EUCLIDEAN, DOT_PRODUCT.

VectorIndex.doc: Contains the configuration settings for a vector index, including the index name, vector attribute, dimensions, distance function, search schema, and projection.

IndexName.doc: The name of the vector index.

SearchSchema.doc: The search schema that defines partition key and inline filter attributes for the vector index.

Projection.doc: Specifies attributes that are copied (projected) from the table into the vector index.

VectorAttribute.doc: The vector attribute configuration for the index.

Dimensions.doc: The number of dimensions in each vector.

DistanceFunction.doc: The distance function used to calculate similarity between vectors.

IndexStatus.doc: The current state of the vector index: CREATING - The index is being created. ACTIVE - The index is ready for use. DELETING - The index is being deleted.

Backfilling.doc: Specifies whether the index is currently backfilling. During backfill, SearchVectors operations might return incomplete results.

IndexSizeBytes.doc: The total size of the vector index, in bytes. Amazon DynamoDB updates this value approximately every six hours. Recent changes might not be reflected in this value.

ItemCount.doc: The number of items indexed in the vector index. Amazon DynamoDB updates this value approximately every six hours. Recent changes might not be reflected in this value.

IndexArn.doc: The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) that uniquely identifies the vector index.

VectorIndexDescription.doc: Contains the current state and configuration of a vector index, including its status, size, item count, and the settings specified when the index was created.

IndexName.doc: The name of the vector index.

VectorAttribute.doc: The vector attribute configuration for the index.

SearchSchema.doc: The search schema that defines partition key and inline filter attributes for the vector index.

Projection.doc: Specifies attributes that are copied (projected) from the table into the vector index.

Dimensions.doc: The number of dimensions in each vector.

DistanceFunction.doc: The distance function used to calculate similarity between vectors.

VectorIndexInfo.doc: Contains the configuration of a vector index as it existed at the time a backup was created.

Create.doc: The configuration for creating a new vector index on the table.

Delete.doc: The configuration for deleting an existing vector index from the table.

VectorIndexUpdate.doc: A vector index to be added to or removed from a table.

ReadUnitsPerSecond.doc: Represents the number of read operations your base table can instantaneously support.

WriteUnitsPerSecond.doc: Represents the number of write operations your base table can instantaneously support.

WarmThroughput.doc: Provides visibility into the number of read and write operations your table or secondary index can instantaneously support. The settings can be modified using the UpdateTable operation to meet the throughput requirements of an upcoming peak event.

PutRequest.doc: A request to perform a PutItem operation.

DeleteRequest.doc: A request to perform a DeleteItem operation.

WriteRequest.doc: Represents an operation to perform - either DeleteItem or PutItem. You can only request one of these operations, not both, in a single WriteRequest. If you do need to perform both of these operations, you need to provide two separate WriteRequest objects.
